gates.gate: Chromium smoke at 390 and 1280 px; smoke_pages; the live preview build on the branch.
gates.status: passed locally; the branch's live preview pending the push: the D17 rule passes on a live build (the 24-hour layer, 2,815 changed pixels in the 160-pixel box at zoom 11, desktop and phone; the hour layer had no value in the box, so its gate is the note) and on the sample build with the real store (14,074 and 14,010 pixels); smoke_pages passes on the live build (every page fits at 288 to 1,440 px, light and dark)
gates.evidence: D17 (the brief's gate B4-7 reads so): tools/smoke_map.py opens each layer at a listed cell with a value at or above 0.25 in, closes the sheet, drags the map if a panel covers the spot, zooms on the spot to zoom 10 or closer (the map's maximum is 11), and requires at least 16 changed pixels in a box of 160 screen pixels around the spot, with the picture hidden in both captures as the control (the whole canvas may not change with it hidden). With no value in the box the note reads 'no values in the box: pixel gate not applicable'. The count is recorded as a note for each size. This pass, the sample build (build --storm-layers --hail-history --sample --hail-store /home/user/hail-b2/out2/joins/hail-store.tar.gz; smoke rc 0, 'Map smoke test passed'): hour desktop 14,074 pixels in the box (zoom 11; 41.95% of the canvas), hour phone 14,074 (27.36%), 24-hour desktop 14,010 (46.45%), 24-hour phone 14,010 (28.40%). The earlier 16-pixel rule counted the whole canvas, and it never zoomed in: the spot's sheet covered the map, so the wheel went to its scrim and the re-check's 365 pixels were taken at zoom 9. The 2 percent rule stays with the dense radar and satellite pictures (tools/smoke_map.py's own checks for those layers).
caveats: D17's figure of 'about 7 by 5 screen pixels' for a 0.01-degree cell at zoom 10 does not match the Web Mercator scale: at 47.5 N a cell is about 3.6 by 5.4 px at zoom 9, 7.3 by 10.8 px at zoom 10 and 14.6 by 21.6 px at zoom 11 (computed). The gate does not depend on the figure, and no document quotes it.
